hypothesis: A Ruzsa modular Golomb ruler with 42 marks, split into seven balanced residue classes modulo 7 and divided by 7, can yield a scope-111 (7,5)-DTS after exhaustive unit multiplier and translation search.
rationale: The DTS literature identifies modular Golomb rulers and residue-class splitting as algebraic construction mechanisms. For prime p=43, the Ruzsa construction gives 42 marks modulo 43*42=1806, exactly enough for seven classes of six marks; modular difference uniqueness guarantees disjoint ordinary differences after the residue-class division. Exhausting the finite symmetry orbit tests this structured family directly rather than sampling arbitrary rows.
expected_information_gain: Determines whether the natural p=43 Ruzsa/Ling algebraic family contains a target witness and records its best attainable linear scope, closing or promoting a literature-backed construction path.
method: Generate the Ruzsa ruler values u_i=43*i+42*g^i mod 1806 for every primitive root g modulo 43. For every unit multiplier and translation modulo 1806, partition transformed values by residue modulo 7, retain balanced six-element classes, sort each class, subtract its minimum, and divide by 7. Validate every resulting seven-row assignment with the repository independent integer verifier; preserve the best scope and any target witnesses.
metric: number of modular rulers, balanced transforms, best verified ordinary DTS scope, target witnesses, and independent validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A verifier-valid split with scope<=111 is exactly a true-objective witness; a best scope above 111 is structured-family evidence only.
kill_condition: Stop at the first independently validated scope-111 witness or after exhaustive enumeration of all primitive roots, unit multipliers, and translations; do not infer global infeasibility from this construction family.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if complete and validator-valid

interpretation: The corrected exact enumeration completed the entire tested Ruzsa/Ling split orbit. Its best independently valid ordinary DTS had scope 195 and no transform reached scope 111, so this algebraic family does not approach the frozen target under the tested construction.
what_was_learned: The natural p=43 Ruzsa modular ruler split is structurally valid but produces ordinary rows with a best scope of 195 across all 12 primitive roots, unit multipliers, and translations. The family is therefore far from the 111 target; the initial Python overhead was an implementation issue and the corrected run supplies the scientific result. No global infeasibility inference is justified.
recommended_next_action: Close this exact Ruzsa/Ling split family; do not spend more compute on its orbit. A future DTS allocation should use a materially different algebraic construction or return to WAITING_FOR_CAPABILITY.
repetition_justification: This is the first modular-ruler algebraic construction tested in the repository. It is not a parameter or seed variation of affine gaps, random catalogs, row packing, or the FPGA reference.
